task:
COLONY PLANNER S4b PART 2: WIRE THE RAVEN LAYOUT IMPORT INTO THE /plan PAGE. apps/web ONLY. NO API, STORAGE-FORMAT, DEPENDENCY OR NETWORK CHANGES.

Authority: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-v3-colony-planner-design.md sections 4.1, 5.3 (belts), 7 (S4b row) and 10 items 3 and 5. Raven Colonial is GPL-3: do NOT copy, port or look up any Raven code. The import reads only the JSON layout file a commander downloads from Raven (their own data). ED-Finder never fetches from Raven's servers.

Already on main: `parseRavenLayout` and `matchRavenBodies` in apps/web/src/lib/features/plan/raven-import.ts (pure, tested); the /plan page (PlanWorkspace.svelte) with its "Import plan" button for ED-Finder's own export format; `resolvePlanLocations` in locations.ts (one location per belt, using the belt's lowest-numbered cluster body as `body_ref`, or `belt:<belt_id>` when the data has no cluster; other clusters and barycentres are hidden); model.ts helpers (`replacePlan`, `rejectInvalidLocations`, `isPlannerSite`, `MAX_SITES`, `MAX_IMPORT_BYTES`).

Files you may change or add (nothing else):
- apps/web/src/lib/features/plan/raven-apply.ts (new) and raven-apply.test.ts (new)
- apps/web/src/lib/features/plan/PlanWorkspace.svelte, plan.css, and the existing PlanWorkspace tests / test host
- apps/web/src/lib/features/plan/__fixtures__/ (new synthetic fixtures only; invented names, no commander names)
- apps/web/cypress/e2e/plan.cy.ts and its fixture folder, only to add one Raven import step (see TESTS)

1. Pure mapping, raven-apply.ts. Export
   `ravenToPlannerModel(result: RavenImportResult, data: PlanBodiesV1): { model: PlannerModel; warnings: { code: string; detail: string }[] }`
   (throw only if `result.ok` is false or `result.system.id64 !== data.system_id64`; the page checks both first).
   - Locations come from `resolvePlanLocations(data)` only. A site or slot row may end up only on one of those `body_ref`s, or Unplaced (`body_ref: null`).
   - Belts first: if a Raven body name is exactly a belt's name, or is `<belt name> Cluster <digits>`, map it to that belt's location `body_ref`. This covers clusters that are hidden in ED-Finder and clusters missing from ED-Finder's data. If the cluster number is not the lowest that ED-Finder has for that belt (or ED-Finder has none), add warning `belt_cluster_moved` naming the Raven body and the belt. The game builds belts only through the first cluster.
   - Otherwise match with `matchRavenBodies` (exact name, case-insensitive, trimmed) and keep the warnings it gives. A match that is not a visible location (a barycentre, or anything `resolvePlanLocations` hides) becomes Unplaced with warning `hidden_body`.
   - Unmatched or ambiguous names become Unplaced. Carry the warnings from `matchRavenBodies`.
   - Sites keep Raven's order. Use status, facility_id, slot_kind and name from the parse result. Each site gets `schema: 'cpe_site_v1'` and a deterministic `site_id` derived from `raven_site_id`, valid under `isPlannerSite`. If an id is reused or invalid, derive a unique id and warn `site_id_changed`. Every produced site must pass `isPlannerSite`. If more than `MAX_SITES` sites remain, keep the first `MAX_SITES` and warn `too_many_sites`.
   - If a facility does not fit its location (`facilityFitsLocation` needs the facility; if the page's facility list is not available to this pure function, take an optional facilities argument), keep the site where Raven put it and warn `facility_location_mismatch`. The evaluator will show it as Blocked with a reason.
   - Slots: give each mapped location `{orbital_slots, surface_slots}` from its Raven slot row. Several Raven rows can map to one belt. Use the row from the lowest-numbered cluster and warn `belt_slots_merged` for the rest. Drop rows for unmatched or hidden bodies with warning `slots_dropped`. The result must satisfy the model's slot validation (null or an integer from 0 to 64).
   - Deterministic: no Date, no randomness, no I/O. The result must pass `rejectInvalidLocations(model, data)`.

2. Page, PlanWorkspace.svelte. Add an "Import from Raven" button next to "Import plan", with its own hidden file input (accept .json; aria-label "Import Raven Colonial layout file"). Then:
   - Over `MAX_IMPORT_BYTES` → the existing action-error message style.
   - JSON.parse failure → "This file is not a Raven Colonial layout (it is not valid JSON)."
   - `parseRavenLayout` not ok → show its first error detail.
   - Bodies not loaded → the same "Wait for the system bodies to load…" error as the existing import.
   - `system.id64` differs → refuse, with no confirm: "This Raven layout is for <name> (<id64>). Open that system's planner to import it."
   - Otherwise build the model and confirm with `window.confirm`: "Replace this system's planner sites and slot counts with <n> sites from Raven Colonial? <u> will be Unplaced and <w> items need checking. The first site becomes the Primary Port." Then apply through `change((current) => replacePlan(current, candidate))`, exactly like the existing import, so the Primary Port protection (RB-0008) is enforced. Show its error if it refuses.
   - After a successful import, announce it in the page's existing polite live region: "<n> sites imported from Raven Colonial." Show the warnings as a dismissible list ("Import notes (<w>)") near the header. Use a `<details>` element or the existing disclosure pattern, each warning's detail as a list item, and a Dismiss button. No colour-only meaning.
   - Never print or store the file's raw contents beyond what the model keeps. Keep the existing "Import plan" behaviour exactly as it is.

TESTS
- raven-apply.test.ts:
  - exact body match;
  - case-insensitive body match;
  - unmatched → Unplaced + warning;
  - ambiguous → Unplaced;
  - barycentre → Unplaced with `hidden_body`;
  - "<belt> Cluster 1" → the belt's location;
  - "<belt> Cluster 3" while ED-Finder has 1–4 → the belt's location + `belt_cluster_moved`;
  - cluster when ED-Finder has no clusters → `belt:<id>`;
  - the belt name itself → the belt's location;
  - slot rows merged for a belt + `belt_slots_merged`;
  - slots for unmatched bodies dropped;
  - duplicate Raven site ids → unique ids + `site_id_changed`;
  - 301 sites → 300 + `too_many_sites`;
  - every produced site passes `isPlannerSite`;
  - the result passes `rejectInvalidLocations`;
  - determinism: the same input twice gives deep-equal output.
- PlanWorkspace component test (existing conventions):
  - upload a synthetic Raven layout for the page's system; confirm; assert the sites appear in order with Unplaced where expected, the live-region text and the notes list;
  - wrong system → the refusal message with no confirm;
  - cancelled confirm → nothing changes;
  - a completed Primary Port that the import would replace → the RB-0008 error and no change.
- Cypress plan.cy.ts: one step that imports a synthetic Raven fixture through the new button, with the intercepts the spec already uses, and checks the site count and one belt site's location. If the spec cannot do this without new intercepts, add the minimal intercept; never weaken existing assertions.

VALIDATION: in apps/web: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test` (report counts), `pnpm build`. SUMMARY: the files changed, the exported function signature, the warning codes, and confirmation that no Raven code was consulted and no other file changed.

A previous attempt at this task stopped at its usage limit before pushing anything, so start fresh from current main.

ADDED FROM THE 2026-10-31 AUDIT, REVISED 2026-11-01 BY THE REVIEWER:
(a) Numeric-id boundary. The file entry point must read the Raven file's ids losslessly. A plain JSON.parse turns numeric 9007199254740993 into 9007199254740992 before raven-import.ts sees it. Either parse the raw text so large integer ids stay exact strings, or reject any numeric id that is not a safe integer with a clear message. Add a test that feeds the raw file TEXT (not a pre-built object) with id 9007199254740993 and checks the result.
(b) Full build-type table from DaftMav. BUILD_TYPES in apps/web/src/lib/features/plan/raven-import.ts maps only 23 Raven build-type names. The owner supplied DaftMav's workbook ("Copy of Colonization Construction v3 (By DaftMav).xlsx", the same workbook apps/api/src/domain/facility_catalogue_v1.json was generated from). Its sheet "Lists", rows 48-159 (columns Structure, Layout Variant, S/O), names every layout. The reviewer joined each Structure to the catalogue template whose `source_structure` equals it (all 112 matched exactly one id) and normalised each Layout Variant to a key (lower case, size suffix " (S)/(M)/(L)" removed, spaces to underscores). All 23 existing entries agree with this table. Replace BUILD_TYPES with exactly these 112 entries, in this order, keeping the existing [facility_id, slot_kind] shape, with a short comment naming the workbook, sheet and rows as the source. Do not consult Raven's code. The keys for the Coriolis, Asteroid Base and Dodecahedron variants and the two Tellus hubs (no_truss, dual_truss, ice, metal, rock, no_truss_dodo, quint_truss, tellus_a, tellus_b) are the normalised DaftMav names and may not be the exact Raven ids; keep them, and leave any other unknown build type on the existing fail-closed path, with a warning that names the Raven type and the site. Add tests: the table has 112 unique keys; every facility_id exists in the planner's facility catalogue (the same source the page and evaluator use); every slot_kind is "orbital" or "surface" as listed; the original 23 keys keep their mappings; and a layout using Phorcys, Nomos, Harmonia, Gaea and Aphrodite imports those sites. If a facility_id in this table is not accepted by the planner (for example a hub or port type the planner model rejects), do not drop it silently: make it Unplaced or skipped with a clear warning and list it in your report.
